newsitem.title: USA: Norfolk Southern says Conrail violated duty.
newsitem.headline: Norfolk Southern says Conrail violated duty.

text.p: Directors of Conrail Inc violated their duties to the company and misled shareholders in agreeing with CSX Corp that it would not consider another company's offer through December 31, 1998, Norfolk Southern Corp said in court documents.
"Put simply, Conrail's directors have agreed to take a two-year leave of absence during what may be the most critical period in Conrail's history," Norfolk Southern said.
"The two-year lock-out is 'ultra vires' (beyond the board's authority) under Pennsylvania law and constitutes a complete abdication of the Conrail directors' duties of loyalty and care."

The charges are contained in documents filed late Friday with the U.S. District Court for Eastern Pennsylvania, in which Norfolk Southern requests an injunction to prevent CSX and Conrail from taking further steps to complete their planned merger.
Norfolk Southern, pursuing a rival bid for Conrail, had indicated its intention on Thursday to challenge the "exclusivity period" during which Conrail agreed not to consider third offers.
The court has scheduled a January 9 hearing on the issue, before U.S. District Judge Donald Van Artsdalen.

Conrail on Thursday said it had extended the exclusivity period from an earlier expiration of July 1997, as part of an increased offer by CSX. The court earlier upheld the shorter expiration period. Conrail has said the new Norfolk Southern challenge lacked merit.
Norfolk Southern said in its court papers the exclusivity provision gives an unfair time advantage to the CSX offer in that its own offer could not be considered for two years.
It said the agreement violates Pennsylvania law in prohibiting Conrail's directors from ending their merger agreement with CSX even if their fiduciary duties would compel them to do otherwise.
It said the pact also would unlawfully bind future directors of Conrail.
